solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Deliberately dodging physical activity

definitions.meaning: missing a class or meeting on purpose, as in cutting a lesson
jumping over a turning rope as exercise or a playground game

explanation.surface: Someone is wilfully avoiding exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both senses: wilfully missing something, and the rope-jumping exercise boxers and children do.

clue.text: Mad about first of seed being thinly scattered

indicators.note: the word for mad goes around the letter taken from seed

parts.note: to go spare is British slang for to go mad with anger

indicators.note: signals taking only the opening letter of seed

explanation.surface: A gardener is furious that the seed has come up patchily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts S, from 'first of seed', inside SPARE; 'go spare' is British slang for getting furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something sparse is meagre, spread thinly with gaps between.

clue.text: Island savings scheme penetrated by foreign character

indicators.note: the savings scheme is entered by the Greek letter, so one sits inside the other

parts.note: an ISA is a British Individual Savings Account
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A tax-free savings plan has been infiltrated by some shady outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a UK tax-free savings account; CHI is the Greek letter, the 'foreign character'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a volcanic island in the Bay of Naples, Italy.

clue.text: In America, game to have drink before dance

indicators.note: the drink comes first, ahead of the dance, in the assembled word

parts.note: punch is a mixed drink served from a bowl
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: An American suggests having a cocktail before heading to the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this is a US playground game in which a large ball is struck with the fist.

clue.text: Reform I saw in modern evolutionary theory

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notes that they have spotted a revision within current evolutionary thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the modern synthesis of natural selection with Mendelian genetics is a theory of evolution.

clue.text: Your compiler's about to stay in the same place

indicators.note: the setter's 'I am' goes around the word for remaining

parts.note: the setter referring to themselves gives I, and 's is 'is' or 'am', giving I'M
to bide is to stay or wait

explanation.surface: A setter announces they are about to remain where they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Your compiler' is the setter, I; with 's it reads I'M, which goes 'about' BIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin term, used in footnotes, means a source is the same one just cited.

clue.text: In Scotland, finely dressed knight's muscularity

parts.note: braw is Scots for fine or handsomely dressed
N is the chess notation for a knight; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A well-turned-out Scottish knight shows off his physique.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: physical strength and muscle, as in brains and bulk.

clue.text: Enfeebled duke, abandoning our country, moved slowly round island

indicators.note: the word duke leaves behind the letters of the nation named next

parts.note: for a British setter, our country is the UK

indicators.note: the verb for moving slowly goes around the island letter

parts.note: crept means moved slowly and quietly

explanation.surface: A frail aristocrat leaves Britain and creeps around some island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke' is used whole, not abbreviated to D, so 'abandoning' strips the British setter's 'our country' from the full word; 'round' wraps the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: worn out and weakened by age or neglect.

clue.text: Greek dramatist's amble round end of green

indicators.note: the word for wandering goes around the letter picked from green

parts.note: to meander is to wander slowly

indicators.note: picks the final letter of green

explanation.surface: A Greek playwright takes a stroll around the village green.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: he was the leading Athenian writer of New Comedy, around 300 BC.

clue.text: What may be grave for missing female singer!

parts.note: a grave accent is a mark over a letter, so grave is one kind

indicators.note: the word for loses a letter, the one standing for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone muses about what might lie in the grave of a lost woman vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' is the accent mark, not a tomb; 'singer' is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the dunnock and its relatives are songbirds of this family.

clue.text: Bird caught on Cornish river to the west

indicators.note: in an across answer, west is the left, so the river comes before the rest

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A bird is netted beside a river in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the west' puts FAL on the left; the Fal is a river in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a swift bird of prey, used in hunting.

clue.text: Instrument identified in general speech outside bar?

indicators.note: the general and speech words sit around the word for bar

parts.note: to lock is to bar a door
a spiel is a glib speech

explanation.surface: A general's address is overheard while standing outside a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is a verb, to fasten; 'outside' wraps the general's speech around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a percussion instrument of tuned metal bars struck with hammers.

clue.text: Ultimately serious desire to be fashionable

indicators.note: at the very end, so the last letter of serious is taken

parts.note: a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: In the end, a deep longing to be stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: smart and stylish, often expensively so.

clue.text: Georgian citizen holds end of rope, having great strength

indicators.note: the citizen word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: an Atlantan lives in Atlanta, capital of the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: picks the final letter of rope

explanation.surface: A burly American from Georgia grips the end of a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgian' is the US state, not the country; Atlanta is its capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: like Atlas, the Titan who bore the heavens on his shoulders, so immensely strong.

clue.text: Sore about Scottish town, she adopts Irish county

indicators.note: turned about, so the word for sore runs backwards

parts.note: raw means sore, as raw skin
Wick is a town in Caithness, northern Scotland

indicators.note: she takes in the abbreviation, so it sits inside her

explanation.surface: An angry woman from a Scottish town takes on an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish county' misleads: 'Irish' is only IR; the county is English, in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a Midlands county of England, home to Stratford-upon-Avon.

clue.text: Breaking ice a lot is — part of one's lifestyle?

definitions.text: Breaking ice a lot is — part of one's lifestyle?

indicators.note: breaking the words up lets their letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting conversation going at parties is a big part of some people's lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer: a party-goer for whom breaking the ice is routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashionable person known for attending parties, where breaking the ice is daily work.

clue.text: It's inclined to go west, protected by allowance

indicators.note: the dying word is sheltered inside the allowance word

parts.note: a grant is an allowance of money
to go west is slang for to die

explanation.surface: Someone tempted to head west is held back by their stipend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go west' is old slang for dying, giving DIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope or incline, so this is the thing that is inclined.

clue.text: Booth, for example, with Charlie and Jenny in?

parts.note: a charlie is British slang for a fool, as is an ass
a jenny is a female donkey, an ass

explanation.surface: Someone named Booth is pictured with two companions inside.
explanation.walkthrough: John Wilkes Booth shot Abraham Lincoln; 'Charlie' is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Booth killed President Lincoln, so he is a political murderer.

clue.text: Dazzling brightness of quiet chap replacing one in home

indicators.note: the new letters take the place of the one letter in the home word

parts.note: a residence is a home
I is the Roman numeral for one
P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
Len is a man's name, standing for any chap

explanation.surface: A quiet man moves into a house, bringing dazzle with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps the I of RESIDENCE for P + LEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: splendour, a brilliant and impressive shining quality.

clue.text: Breed of sheep doctor keeps in old Ireland

indicators.note: the doctor word keeps the old name for Ireland inside it

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
Erin is a poetic old name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A vet keeps some sheep in the Ireland of long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sheep breed prized for its fine wool.

clue.text: Tight-fisted type withholding pounds from girl

indicators.note: the girl's name holds back a letter, leaving it out

parts.note: Melanie is a girl's name
L stands for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A stingy person refuses to hand over money owed to a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal noun for a miser, someone ungenerous with money.

clue.text: Identification of disease in dogs is a diversion

indicators.note: the letters are diverted from their order into a new one

explanation.surface: A vet notes that an illness in dogs is a distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the doctor's or vet's determination of which illness is present.

clue.text: Old railwaymen with points to look after

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a former British trade union
S and E are compass points

explanation.surface: Retired rail workers bring up some points to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUR was Britain's National Union of Railwaymen, merged away in 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to care for or tend someone, as a carer does.

clue.text: Murder victim given grave at last in Poplar?

parts.note: Abel, killed by his brother Cain in Genesis

indicators.note: the final letter of grave is taken

explanation.surface: A murdered man is finally buried in Poplar, a district of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poplar' looks like the East London district, but it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the white poplar tree goes by this name.

clue.text: Make certain council leader is excluded from blame

indicators.note: a letter is left out of the blame word

parts.note: to censure is to blame formally

indicators.note: the leading, first letter of council

explanation.surface: A council's head makes sure they escape criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to guarantee or make sure that something happens.

clue.text: Green pigment, one I delivered first in commercial vehicle

indicators.note: these letters go inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a van is a commercial vehicle

indicators.note: the delivered word comes first, ahead of the second I

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to rid is to deliver or free from

explanation.surface: A delivery driver's van holds a tin of green paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts RID before the second I; 'delivered' means freed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bluish-green pigment made from chromium oxide.

clue.text: Gentle 22's offer?

definitions.meaning: one who tends or looks after, as the answer to 22 does
to put forward formally, as a bid

explanation.surface: A carer makes a kind proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: soft or kind; one who tends; and a formal bid or offer.

clue.text: Unaccompanied song not all finding full of merriment

parts.note: a glee is a part-song for unaccompanied voices
some is fewer than all

explanation.surface: Part of a choir's a cappella piece is found to be joyful.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic adjective meaning merry and joyful.
